retryIdempotency.statement: AP2 v0.2 names double spend as a threat. Its mitigation places a MUST on the Shopping Agent not to sign or present overlapping closed mandates from one open mandate without a rejection receipt for the earlier one, and gives verifiers a MAY to reject overlapping mandates. Each closed Payment Mandate carries a transaction_id that is the hash of the checkout it pays for. Whether the instrument beneath can move value twice on an identical resubmit is not answered at this layer.

The Machine Payments Protocol Lightning draft states that settlement is final once the preimage is revealed and that the preimage is not revealed until the HTLC resolves.

retryIdempotency.value: same preimage: not accepted twice (atomic consume-once, MUST); another payment to an already paid hash: MAY be accepted (BOLT 4); deduplication: optional transferId (Spark wallet)
retryIdempotency.statement: The core draft requires single-use proofs and the Lightning method draft requires that a consumed challenge is never accepted again, with acceptance and invalidation atomic. BOLT 4 says a final node whose payment hash has already been paid MAY succeed in accepting the HTLC, so another payment to the same hash is not prevented at the protocol layer. On the Spark path, payLightningInvoice takes an optional transferId for retrying the same logical payment, and the docs tell integrators not to create another payment because the original call threw.

ambiguityBound.statement: Protocol half (stated): BOLT 7 has the origin compute HTLC expiries backward from the destination, each hop advertises the blocks it subtracts, and the delta contributes to the time funds are unavailable if the payment fails; BOLT 2 gates failure on downstream resolution and derives an upper allowance in blocks from stated assumptions. Operator half (not stated as a bound available to the agent): on the Spark path the hosted Lightning payment provider builds the route; payLightningInvoice returns no expiry field, the Spark overview says operators lock the sender leaves until a specified time, and the wallet guide says the swap expiry is not a guaranteed refund time.

The Spark overview describes a Lightning payment provider that pays the invoice and submits proof to the Spark operators. At the protocol layer the routing error channel is documented as unreliable, and no document read describes a public arbiter for a Lightning payment.

value.initiatedBy: payer node (spends the HTLC after its timeout) or a downstream node (fails the HTLC back)
value.conditions: Protocol layer: the HTLC was not fulfilled with the preimage; the payer can cancel after a given time, and nodes must fail the incoming HTLC once its cltv_expiry is reached.

Operator layer (Spark): if the specified lock time expires without proof of payment, the operators unlock the sender leaves; the wallet guide states the swap expiry is not a guaranteed refund time and that the SDK has no public client cancellation method for an in-flight send.

Out-of-protocol only: the Lightning method draft states settled payments cannot be refunded through the payment channel; mpp.dev states refunds in the charge flow are out-of-protocol. The Lightning draft makes the credential source field optional and forbids servers from requiring it, so the protocol does not supply a refund destination.

restitutionKinds.statement: After settlement (preimage revealed) no in-protocol return path exists in the documents read; the method draft says so explicitly. Before settlement, the HTLC can be cancelled or failed back at the protocol layer, and on the Spark path the operator lock lapses at a specified time. Any refund of a settled charge is out-of-protocol and at the payee discretion.

observerPrivacyExposure.value: protocol layer: no public payment ledger is described; forwarding hops see the amount to forward and their adjacent nodes, not the origin (ephemeral key) or full route; the invoice carries the payee node public key and a description; the receipt reference (payment hash) is described as publicly shareable. operator layer (Spark): new wallets have privacy off, so public clients can query Bitcoin balances and transfer history unless the owner enables privacy mode
observerPrivacyExposure.statement: BOLT 4 states intermediate nodes cannot learn route members beyond their predecessor and successor, and that hops see an ephemeral key for the origin in place of its identity; each hop payload carries the amount to forward. BOLT 11 invoices carry the payee node public key and a payment description. The Lightning method draft calls the payment hash a publicly shareable receipt identifier. Spark states new wallets start with privacy off and public clients can query their Bitcoin balances and transfer history.

feeBearer.statement: The Tempo charge method draft makes the fee bearer a per-challenge choice: with methodDetails.feePayer false or omitted the client sets the fee token and arranges payment of the fee; with feePayer true the server commits to paying the fee and may recover the cost through pricing. The Tempo fee specification (chain layer, operator Tempo Labs) states that without a fee payer signature the sender pays, and that a fee payer signature authorizes a third party to pay; fees go to the block proposer.

retryIdempotency.value: identical credential: rejected (single-use proof, MUST); freshly signed transaction: a distinct transaction at the chain layer; second client broadcast in push mode: not addressed; deduplication: single-use challenge (protocol), replay store (mppx SDK)
retryIdempotency.statement: The core draft requires single-use proof semantics and concurrent-request protection, and the charge intent draft requires each challenge id to be single-use; the Tempo method draft names chain ID binding, nonce consumption and validity windows. At the chain layer TIP-1009 states that a transaction hash cannot execute twice but that changing validBefore produces a different hash, so a freshly signed transaction is a distinct transaction. In pull mode the server broadcasts, so another credential for a consumed challenge is rejected before broadcast; in push mode the client broadcasts before presenting the credential, and no document read says whether a second client-broadcast transaction for the same challenge is prevented. The mppx SDK (operator layer) claims transaction hashes and proof challenge IDs in a replay store.

ambiguityBound.statement: The Tempo Transaction carries an optional valid_before expiration timestamp that the payer signs, and the Tempo charge method draft has the client sign with validBefore no later than the challenge expires auth-param, within which the server may submit. TIP-1009 expiring-nonce transactions require validBefore and reject transactions outside a protocol maximum window.

outcomeKnowledge.statement: In pull mode the server broadcasts the signed transaction and reports success through a Payment-Receipt carrying the transaction hash, so knowledge at submission passes through the payee; the Tempo chain documentation then states that finalized blocks can be queried through standard JSON-RPC and that a public explorer shows transactions and accounts, so the arbiter is readable without the payee. In push mode the client broadcasts and can read the chain itself.

value.conditions: Out-of-protocol: the Machine Payments Protocol defines no refund protocol; for the charge flow the server may send funds back to the address in the credential source field by an ordinary on-chain transfer.

Pull mode only: a client-signed transaction that the server does not broadcast before its valid_before passes is rejected by the chain, so no value moves; this is a lapse, not a return of settled value.

restitutionKinds.statement: At the protocol layer the charge intent draft states reversibility is method-dependent and neither the core nor the Tempo method draft defines a refund. The mpp.dev refunds page (operator layer) states that refunds in the charge flow are out-of-protocol transfers back to the client. The chain documentation states that finalized blocks cannot be reverted, so no reversal or chargeback path exists at the settlement layer in the documents read.

observerPrivacyExposure.statement: The Tempo documentation states that on Tempo Mainnet anyone can read any account balance and that the public explorer shows transactions, accounts and token activity. The method draft settles by TIP-20 transfer or transferWithMemo calls and defines an optional bytes32 memo; the mpp.dev Tempo charge page states the mppx client adds a challenge-bound attribution memo to the primary transfer. The core draft asks payment methods to support pseudonymous options where possible.

offlineVerifiability.value: by an optional extension: a receipt signed by the resource server, EIP-712 on this network, with the signer address recoverable from the signature and no network call; limits: signer authority is a separate check with no mandated mechanism; the transaction reference is omitted by default; the extension is optional and not yet stable; the settle response itself is unsigned
offlineVerifiability.statement: The x402 Offer and Receipt extension, an optional addition to x402, lets the settlement response carry a receipt signed by the resource server on success. On this network the signer address is recovered from an EIP-712 signature with no network call. Three limits are stated in the extension: a valid signature does not establish that the key may sign for the service, and no mechanism for establishing that is mandated (some of the listed routes are network lookups); the receipt is the resource server's own statement and by default omits the transaction reference; and the extension is optional, with its wire shape not yet stable. The settle response itself is unsigned.

feeBearer.value: the account named as fee payer: the resource server or a third-party facilitator; recovery: not stated
feeBearer.statement: The exact-on-Solana scheme assigns the network fee to the fee-payer account, which may be the merchant or a third-party facilitator, and restricts that account to paying the fee. Solana documentation states the fee is deducted from the fee payer and is charged even if the transaction fails. No document read says the fee is recovered from either party.

finalityModelClass.statement: The Solana RPC overview defines three named commitment levels (processed, confirmed, finalized) that state how finalized a block must be, with processed described as still able to be rolled back. The x402 specification does not define a finality class.

retryIdempotency.value: identical transaction: executes once (network deduplication); re-signed transaction before blockhash expiry: both can be accepted; deduplication: memo nonce and settlement cache (facilitator), optional payment-identifier key (x402 extension)
retryIdempotency.statement: The x402 SVM scheme states that Solana deduplication makes a resubmitted transaction execute once, while the facilitator could still report success to each caller, and specifies a settlement cache as a mitigation. Solana documentation states that re-signing before the original blockhash expires can lead to both transactions being accepted.

ambiguityBound.statement: The signed transaction carries a recent blockhash and expires when that blockhash is no longer recent; Solana documentation says a dropped transaction can be discarded once the blockhash is older than lastValidBlockHeight, and that an expired transaction will never be processed. The x402 scheme can pass lastValidBlockHeight as an informational hint that is not part of the transaction, so the client computes the bound.

outcomeKnowledge.statement: The settlement response travels from the fee-paying party to the resource server and then to the client. The x402 SVM scheme notes the facilitator could report success to several callers for one transfer. Solana documentation describes getSignatureStatuses for reading a signature status from a node, and warns that a network error or malformed facilitator response is not proof of payment.

restitutionKinds.statement: The x402 exact scheme states that it defines no refund and leaves any remedy to the resource server. The SVM scheme, the core specification and the Solana x402 and facilitator pages define no refund, reversal, chargeback, dispute or cancellation path for an exact payment.

observerPrivacyExposure.value: Payer identifier: public ledger address (the client signer and source token account; the fee-payer address is also public). Amount: visible; transactions are described as fully auditable and amount confidentiality is an opt-in Token-2022 extension the exact scheme does not name. Metadata: a Memo instruction carrying extra.memo or a random nonce, recorded in transaction logs. Linkable on the public ledger: yes.
observerPrivacyExposure.statement: Solana documentation states that its public ledger makes every transaction, token account and mint auditable, that memos are recorded on chain and visible in logs, and that privacy is provided by application-level tools. The x402 exact scheme requires a TransferChecked transfer and a Memo instruction, and reports the payer as a public address.

offlineVerifiability.value: by an optional extension: a receipt signed by the resource server, EIP-712 with a constant chainId that the extension states covers Solana; limits: signer authority is a separate check with no mandated mechanism; the transaction reference is omitted by default; the extension is optional and not yet stable; without it, a transaction signature checked by a node query
offlineVerifiability.statement: The x402 Offer and Receipt extension, an optional addition to x402, lets the settlement response carry a receipt signed by the resource server on success, and states that its EIP-712 signing works on non-EVM networks including Solana. Three limits are stated in the extension: a valid signature does not establish that the key may sign for the service, and no mechanism for establishing that is mandated (some of the listed routes are network lookups); the receipt is the resource server's own statement and by default omits the transaction reference; and the extension is optional, with its wire shape not yet stable. Without the extension the agent holds a transaction signature, which is checked by querying a node.

feeBearer.value: facilitator, as the transaction source account; recovery: not stated in the specification
feeBearer.statement: The Stellar exact scheme has the facilitator rebuild the transaction with its own account as source, and that account pays the fee; the paying agent signs an authorization entry, not the transaction. The specification does not say whether the cost is recovered; the OpenZeppelin Channels documentation for the service used by the hosted Built on Stellar facilitator says fees are paid by the service and that the service is free to use.

retryIdempotency.value: identical authorization entry: cannot apply twice (nonce consumed by the host); freshly signed entry: not prevented; deduplication: Soroban nonce (protocol), optional payment-identifier key (x402 extension)
retryIdempotency.statement: The authorization entry the agent signs carries a nonce unique per address until its expiration ledger, and the host verifies and consumes it, so the same entry cannot apply twice. Nothing read prevents the agent from signing another entry with a new nonce. The x402 payment-identifier extension, published in the canonical repository, offers an optional idempotency key that resource servers and facilitators may use.

offlineVerifiability.value: receipt: defined by the same optional extension, signed by the resource server; checkable offline on a Stellar network: not settled by the documents read; operator documentation: does not mention the extension
offlineVerifiability.statement: The x402 Offer and Receipt extension defines an optional receipt signed by the resource server; the settle response of the x402 v2 specification is unsigned. Whether that receipt can be checked offline on a Stellar network is not settled by the documents read: one section of the extension limits EIP-712 receipts to EVM networks while another states that EIP-712 signing works on non-EVM networks, and a JWS receipt needs a DID URL resolved by a method the extension does not fix. The Stellar x402 page read does not mention the extension.
